A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UNIFEWS and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables. Inspection includes all of v1 and v2's Appendices A–C; retained material can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original node-classification, runtime, operation-count, sparsification and sensitivity experiments in Section 6, alongside empirical approximation analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results in Section 5 and adds backbone, dataset, uncertainty and synthetic-graph results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 now explicitly excludes v=u from the neighbor loop, whereas v1 traverses the self-looped edge set. This changes the written treatment of self-connections. The underlying magnitude thresholds, progressive edge removal, weight pruning and skip initialization remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 retains the six original datasets and adds physics plus four GenCAT synthetic graphs with controlled degree and attribute distributions. This extends dataset and input-condition coverage without introducing a new downstream prediction task; arxiv was already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Figure 12 adds unpruned GCNII and GraphSAGE reference curves for their UNIFEWS variants. The competing sparsification methods in matched experiments remain GLT, GEBT, CGP, DSpar, Random/RAN, NDLS and NIGCN; no new competing pruning algorithm is evaluated.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce GraphSAGE and 32-layer GCNII evaluations, a 7-by-7 joint-threshold grid, and controlled GenCAT experiments using alpha=2.1/2.9 and sigma=0.1/1.0. These substantially extend evaluation settings. Shared experiments retain their stated training budgets, metrics and default configurations; fuller split reporting does not establish changed splits.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds joint-threshold heatmaps testing interactions between edge and weight pruning, and synthetic experiments testing the threshold–sparsity relationship under controlled distributions. Existing approximation-error, oversmoothing, operation-breakdown and depth-sensitivity analyses are retained, often relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: V2 first reports shaded variability bands for GCN/GAT on cora in Figure 13 and discusses approximately 1–3% 'variance.' Neither the run count nor the statistical meaning of the bands is specified, so this establishes added uncertainty reporting, not additional runs or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Figures 11, 12, 14 and 16 add substantial accuracy, joint-threshold and synthetic-graph results. These are additional findings, not demonstrated improvements on shared settings. V1 Table 3 and v2 Table 1 retain the same numerical results, including SGC+UNIFEWS on papers100m at 63.1% accuracy and 192.4 seconds.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.2 and Appendix B.3 add power-law degree and Gaussian embedding assumptions and derive an explicit sparsity-dependent threshold and spectral-error bound. V2 also states an L-round iterative bound as Proposition 4.4. Most earlier smoothing and propagation arguments are retained in Appendix B; their relocation is not new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: unified entry-wise graph/weight sparsification, progressive compression across layers, bounded approximation, applicability to iterative and decoupled GNNs, and comparable accuracy with roughly 10–20-fold operation reduction and up to 100-fold acceleration. Added evidence supports this existing contribution scope.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly identifies heterophily as a limitation because large messages may be unhelpful, requiring changes to smoothing and pruning. Appendix C also attributes GCNII instability to amplified approximation error and GAT weight sensitivity to concentrated attention values. The original oversmoothing and reciprocal-sparsity interpretations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access link, validation/test proportions alongside training splits, and details of synthetic generation and additional backbone configurations. These improve documentation without establishing changes to retained experiments. Hardware and shared training defaults were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds literature supporting distributional assumptions, GenCAT, additional backbones and recent spectral sparsification, including discussion of Ding et al. (2025). Appendix A distinguishes simplification from sampling/coarsening modifications. The principal positioning against static graph pruning and joint compression remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites and condenses the abstract and introduction, combines preliminaries with related work, reorganizes algorithm and theory exposition, and moves detailed literature, proofs and experiments into Appendices A–C. The title and author line also change.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document format and extensively redistributes displays. V1 Figure 4 is split into v2 Figures 3 and 10; notation and theoretical-analysis displays move to appendices. Algorithms gain highlighting, tables are restructured, and new backbone plots, uncertainty bands, heatmaps and synthetic-graph figures are added.

improvement.justification: Broader backbone validation, controlled synthetic experiments, fuller reproducibility information and explicit applicability limitations improve support and transparency. The gains are bounded: shared benchmark results remain unchanged, uncertainty bands lack an estimation definition and run counts, and Theorem 4.2 states its threshold relation more generally than the large-threshold approximation derived in Appendix B.3 supports. The revision therefore provides useful but limited overall improvement.
